summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Located primary sources for labour approvals by destination (MoLESS Nepal Labour Migration Report 2024 covering FY2022/23-FY2023/24; DoFE yearly progress reports for later FYs), GCC host-country stocks (GLMM database), and Census 2021 absentee stocks (the only official source that includes India). No values retrieved; destination concentration (HHI, top-k shares, GCC+Malaysia share) and sector/skill composition are pending. Two 2026 disruptions are flagged for verification from official texts: the DoFE suspension of labour approvals for Gulf/Middle East destinations from March 2026 with later partial resumption, and the Malaysia FWCMS recruitment-agency dispute (August-September 2026).

findings.claim: Q1: Labour approvals by destination (each GCC state and Malaysia), new vs re-entry, latest four Nepal FYs.
findings.note: Required: DoFE country-wise approval counts FY2022/23-FY2025/26 (23A-L01, 23A-L02).

findings.claim: Q1: Destination concentration of labour approvals (HHI 0-10000; top-1 and top-3 shares; GCC+Malaysia share).
findings.note: Computed from the counts above once ingested.

findings.claim: Q1: Sector / skill composition of approvals by destination.
findings.note: Required: DoFE skill-level or occupation tabulation by country (if published in Labour Migration Report 2024); GLMM host-country employment by sector and nationality group. If DoFE does not tabulate sector by country, record as data gap.

findings.claim: Q1: Migrant stock by destination including India (Census 2021 absentees) and GCC host-country counts of Nepali nationals.
findings.note: Required: Census 2021 absent population by country (23A-L06); GLMM tables (23A-L04). Stock, not flow; different reference dates.

findings.claim: Q1 context: Effect of the 2026 suspension of approvals for Gulf/Middle East destinations on FY2025/26 approvals.
findings.note: Required: official decision text (dates, destinations covered, re-entry vs new) and DoFE monthly approvals for FY2025/26. News leads 23A-L07/L08/L09 only locate the event.

findings.claim: Q1 context: Effect of Malaysia's 2026 FWCMS agency-listing dispute on approvals to Malaysia.
findings.note: Required: DoFE/MoLESS notice and Malaysian Ministry of Human Resources statement; monthly approvals to Malaysia.

findings.claim: Labour approvals (flows) and absentee/host-country counts (stocks) are separate series and are never summed or converted without a documented attrition/return assumption.
Concentration is measured by HHI (unit index, 0-10000) and top-k shares (unit percent), computed separately for new approvals and re-entry approvals, following 16B-A1.

data_gaps: DoFE country-wise approval tables for FY2024/25 and FY2025/26 not located as direct files (only the yearly-report archive page).
Sector/occupation of approvals by destination may not be published by DoFE; GLMM sector tables cover nationality groups rather than Nepal specifically for most GCC states.
India-bound migration is not captured by DoFE; only Census 2021 stock and NLSS IV household data exist.
Irregular migration via third countries (e.g. through India) is unrecorded in DoFE data.

Wage levels by destination and occupation: no official Nepal source located; host-country wage tables (e.g. GASTAT labour force survey for Saudi Arabia) not yet located as leads because the search budget was exhausted.
Official decision texts for the 2026 suspension and resumption were not located; only news reports.

assumptions.text: Nepal fiscal year (mid-July to mid-July) is the basis for DoFE series; host-country series remain on their native calendar/census basis and are not converted.
Re-entry (renewal) approvals are reported separately because they reflect continued employment rather than new outflows.

challenges.text: Agree with 16B challenge on EXP-02: India must be added as a stock-only counterparty; propose that EXP-02 value be defined as two metrics (flow HHI from DoFE, stock HHI from Census 2021) rather than one.
Labour-supply parameters using DoFE approvals as 'emigration' will undercount India-bound and irregular migrants; use Census 2021 absentee stock for population accounting.
The 2026 Gulf approval suspension and Malaysia agency dispute are candidate stress events for S01/S05-type scenarios; request red-team check once official texts are retrieved.

uncertainty: High. No destination or sector values were retrieved in r1. The main structural uncertainty is coverage: DoFE excludes India and irregular migration, and GCC host-country data have mixed vintages and rarely break out Nepali nationals. 2026 disruptions are known only from news reports and are unverified.
